name: IEC AND-OR-invert element
summary: Two & elements embedded in a ≥1 element with negated output, drawn as one compound IEC AND-OR-invert symbol.
description: The IEC system draws an AND-OR-invert as several & elements abutted against the left side of a ≥1 element, whose output is negated. Because the common line between the & and ≥1 parts is perpendicular to the signal flow, each & element is understood to feed one input of the OR.

AOI structures appear in older TTL-based control boards and in some gate-array documentation. On a drawing they compress several gates into one symbol, so the reader should expand the function mentally as the complement of a sum of products before checking a truth table.
The compound symbol does not show internal timing or whether unused AND inputs are tied. Unused inputs on the physical device must be handled as the datasheet requires.
readingNotes: Read the embedded & elements as product terms feeding the ≥1 element.
Remember the final negation at the output.
drawingChecklist: Abut the & elements cleanly to the ≥1 outline.
Show the tie-off for unused inputs.
distinction: Separate AND gates wired to a NOR gate perform the same function but are drawn as distinct elements with visible interconnections.
